Retired, married White man in the US South (65+, some college) with conservative Republican leanings and low religious attendance. Motivated by avoiding mistakes and losses as much as by achieving goals, he aspires to be a good neighbor who listens, gets along, and helps others, while recognizing he needs more patience.

A young white male in the US South (some college, full-time, mid income), conservative/Republican and agnostic with low religious involvement. He’s socially reserved and blunt, not especially accommodating, and tends to be guarded and skeptical of others’ motives; he’s comfortable keeping resources for himself and is unlikely to trust or reciprocate in one-shot exchanges. Emotionally, he’s moody and stress-sensitive with notable depressive tendencies and a shaky, uncertain self-concept, which can undercut motivation and follow-through despite generally solid self-discipline when structure is present. He strongly prefers clear rules, certainty, and quick closure over ambiguity, and he doesn’t enjoy effortful thinking for its own sake—often relying on intuition—yet he can reason well on structured logic problems and adapt to novel tasks. Decision-wise he’s moderately impatient, average on risk/loss sensitivity, and somewhat spendthrift/impulse-prone, with only moderate numeracy/financial habits. Values mix self-advancement and relationships, with a streak of wanting to stand out; he also shows a surprisingly strong pro-environment tilt. He aspires to “win” via intelligence and tactics, feels he should be a hardworking grinder, and sees himself as capable but prone to pleasure-seeking and weak willpower.

Midwestern white male in his 20s, some college, agnostic and politically independent/moderate, living in a 4-person household; currently unemployed despite high income. Married Hispanic man (30–49) in the US South with postgraduate education, high income, and full-time work; very conservative Republican and weekly churchgoer. Values simplicity/minimalism and shows some pro-environment leanings, while being low on expressed empathy; highly attuned to social expectations and image, with a somewhat uncertain self-concept and a strong focus on being hardworking, successful, humble, and family-committed.

Married White woman in her 50s–early 60s in the Western US, associate’s degree, moderate income and currently unemployed; politically liberal/Democrat and nonreligious. Emotionally steady overall but with elevated anxiety; empathetic, moderately environmentally minded, not strongly novelty-seeking or uniqueness-driven, and prefers a comfortable, non-minimalist lifestyle.

White married woman in her late 60s living in the US South, moderate Democrat with some college, mid–upper income, and part-time work; attends religious services weekly and values community. She wants to be stronger and more confident like her daughter, but often feels she needs support and direction to follow through.

Middle-aged married white woman in the Northeast, self-employed with a high-school education and solid middle income; politically moderate/independent and culturally Catholic but non-practicing. Financially somewhat cautious and risk-averse, with a tendency to feel pain spending money, and she may benefit from simple, concrete options and reassurance rather than complex tradeoffs.

White male (30–49) in the US South; postgraduate-educated, full-time employed, moderate/independent, Roman Catholic and attends weekly; never married and lives in a large household. Midwestern Black male in his 50s–60s, postgraduate-educated, self-employed, single, atheist, and politically liberal/Democrat.
